subject: Post-call: Competitive bakeoff — sprint ops & recommended tests
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datapulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Competitive bakeoff — sprint ops & recommended tests

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so your team has a clear plan for the vendor bakeoff. Short bullets first, then the test plan we propose.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Inconsistent tail latency on long-context prompts (p95 spikes during bursts)
- Unit cost for conversational retrieval flows is higher than expected
- Need predictable behavior if a primary model becomes unavailable (graceful fallback)

Goals you shared:
- Maintain p95 < 800ms for short chat queries and p95 < 1.2s for long-context retrievals
- Reduce per-conversation inference cost by ~30% vs current baseline
- Validate an autoscaling profile that doesn’t overspend on 99th percentile traffic

Decision criteria we agreed to put at the top of the matrix:
1) Latency SLOs & variance (p50/p95/p99)
2) Model quality on your in-domain prompts (accuracy + hallucination checks)
3) Cost predictability (unit economics + burst behavior)
4) Reliability & fallback policies (model variants, region failover)
5) Operability: metrics, tracing, request-level cost breakdown
6) Security & compliance constraints (log retention, VPC options)

Proposed bakeoff tests (we recommend a 10-day sprint):
- Test A: Short-chat steady-state (5k requests/day) — measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost
- Test B: Long-context throughput (2k sessions with 8k token context) — observe KV cache and memory behavior
- Test C: Prefix-caching stress (replay heavy prefixes) — verify prefix/KV cache hit rates and latency improvements
- Test D: Quantized variant A/B (float16 vs 4-bit) — measure quality delta and cost per token
- Test E: Failure injection — throttle primary model for 30s windows and observe fallback behavior

Attachments: I attached a proposed test matrix and a concise runbook describing measurement points and expected artifacts.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the 10-day window and which tests to prioritize (reply with preferred start date).
2) We provision a sandbox with isolated capacity for the run (no production impact).
3) We'll send the test payloads and a short script to replay your sample queries.

If acceptable, can we target Tuesday 2027-04-19 for a kickoff?

Thanks — I’ll loop in SEs after you confirm dates.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bakeoff-test-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: runbook-notes.pdf (pdf)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datapulse.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@datapulse.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive bakeoff — sprint ops & recommended tests

Thanks Stephanie — this is great and aligns with what we need. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can commit to the 10-day window; preference for starting 2027-04-26 rather than the 19th (internal calendar).
- For Test D (quantized variants), can you confirm which model families you’ll include? We want at least one stronger open LLM and one smaller quantized candidate.
- On the failure-injection test: procurement wants assurance that fallback models won’t route sensitive PII to external loggers — can you include the logging/retention settings in the runbook?

Cc'ing Procurement so they can start the quick compliance check.

— Liam
Director, Platform Engineering
DataPulse

Looping in a quick internal note before we reply to Liam:
- Recommended model slate for Test D: redwood-gpt-3.5-rl (float16), open-llm-7B (4-bit quant), and a mid-size 13B quant candidate (customer-provided weights if they want).
- For logging: we’ll use session-level traces with PII redaction and offer a no-logs option in the sandbox. Will add explicit retention settings to the runbook (7/30/90 days options).
- SE availability: I can host the kickoff 2027-04-26-28 to get initial measurement runs; full sprint can be 04/26–05/05.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Competitive bakeoff — sprint ops & recommended tests

Liam — thanks, we’ll proceed with your preferred dates. Confirming the plan and a few concrete artifacts we’ll deliver before kickoff: 

1) Finalized test matrix (attached) with measurement fields and pass/fail criteria.
2) Sandbox provisioning checklist (networking, creds, VPC options) and an opt-out no-logs mode.
3) Model slate for A/B: redwood-gpt-3.5-rl (fp16), open-llm-7b-q4 (4-bit), and a 13B quant candidate.
4) A small script + sample payloads to replay 3k representative sessions (we’ll include a README).

Please confirm the kickoff date as 2027-04-26 and which of the two retention windows you prefer (30 days or 90 days) so Procurement can sign off. Once we have that we’ll open a HubSpot activity (I attached the HubSpot link in related_links).

If Procurement prefers, we can toggle logging to store only request metadata (no prompt/response) during failure-injection tests.

Best,
Stephanie
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
